text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: PAGER fired for service=queue-mediator (high queue length) — alert: 'hotpath queue length > 95% sustained 2min' — incident link: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345 :rotating_light:

incident-bot: Summary: autoscaler not increasing worker count for hotpath cluster 'hp-us-east-3', queue growth observed. Metrics: qlen=18k (threshold 5k), p50 latency 2.1s, rejected reqs 4.2%.

sarah_oncall: acked on PD, taking initial triage. Seeing many 429s from the frontend. Investigating autoscaler logs now.

jake_sre: on it — looking at scale-controller logs. Quick grep shows repeated errors: "scale-loop: insufficient capacity: cloud quota hit". Suspect node quota exhaustion in us-east-3 cloud account.

maya_runtime: confirm kvcache warmup is also thrashing; many cold prefixes causing synchronous disk reads. Could be amplifying queue. Dumping top prefixes to see hotkeys.

oliver_prod: any customer visible impact? Support mentions a cluster of customers reporting slow completions, some timeouts. Prioritize high-traffic product routes.

emma_support: getting an incident from a mid-market customer (acct: AcmeApps) seeing timeouts on embedding API. Marked sev=2; they rely on dedicated latency. Sharing their request IDs in DM.

sarah_oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) open manual scale override to spin additional worker nodes, 2) put temporary rate-limit on non-critical ingestion routes, 3) roll a fallback to a cheaper model variant for >= 90th percentile requests. Who can execute 1?

jake_sre: I can do manual spinup. Running command to increase pool:

jake_sre: ```bash
# manual override: add 8 nodes to hp-us-east-3 pool
redwoodctl pool scale --pool hp-us-east-3 --add-nodes 8 --reason "manual emergency spinup"
```

jake_sre: Kicking that now. Cloud API returning "quota exceeded" for 4 of 8 requests. Looks like provider account has a hard quota.

maya_runtime: while that runs, I'll enable aggressive KV prefix caching for hot prefixes and enable short-term writeback cache to reduce cold reads. Patch config snippet: ```
kvcache.hot_prefix_cache.enabled = true
kvcache.hot_prefix_cache.ttl = 600s
```

sarah_oncall: Good. Also put a temporary routing rule: send <10k qps of experimental batch jobs to a reserve pool 'hp-reserve-1' to relieve the hotpath. Can someone create that route?

oliver_prod: I can create the route; need approval on impact: will increase latency for those jobs ~300ms but reduces tail. Approving.

emma_support: Notifying AcmeApps that we're mitigating and will update in 10m.

jake_sre: Manual spinup partial success: 4 nodes added, 4 failed due to quota. I've opened a ticket with cloud provider support (ticket #CLD-9876) and requested quota emergency increase. Meanwhile I'm rebalancing pods across the 4 newly provisioned nodes.

jake_sre: ```
# reassign hotpath dispatcher to new nodes
kubectl get pods -n hp -l app=dispatcher -o wide
kubectl cordon node-123 && kubectl drain node-123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl apply -f hp-rebalance.yaml
```

maya_runtime: kvcache patch applied and hot prefix cache started. Observing ~18% drop in synchronous KV reads in the last 90s. Nice.

sarah_oncall: Rate limit applied to experimental ingestion routes (200rps global). Monitoring effect on queue depth.

incident-bot: alert update: qlen dropped from 18k -> 9.2k in 4m after partial spinup and cache changes. p50 latency -> 1.3s. Reject rate -> 1.6%.

oliver_prod: Product asks if we can enable graceful fallback model for premium customers only — reduces cost but keeps latency. Is that safe?

maya_runtime: We can route premium customers to a pinned optimized variant (quantized) with fewer resources. Will add a per-customer route. Takes ~3m to stage.

emma_support: AcmeApps updated: they report significant improvement in request success rate. Thank you.

jake_sre: Cloud support responded: quota increase approved for 6 additional instances, ETA ~7m for provisioning. Once they spin up I'll add them. For now we've stabilized but not fully recovered.

sarah_oncall: Next steps: - keep PD on for 30m - monitor qlen and reject% - follow up with infra about quota planning - postmortem owner? Volunteer?

oliver_prod: I'll own postmortem and coordinate customer comms.

maya_runtime: Adding an action: add a safety fallback in scale-controller to detect repeated quota errors and proactively shift traffic to reserve regions before queue hits critical. I'll draft an RFC after incident.

jake_sre: Confirming new nodes arrived, scaling up completed. qlen now 2.8k, p50 0.9s. Closing immediate mitigation.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: incident ACK -> RESOLVED (auto: metrics recovered). PD link: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345/resolved

sarah_oncall: Good job everyone. I'll open a follow-up thread for RCA and add timeline + logs. Thanks for the quick spins and cache tweaks. :thumbsup:

oliver_prod: Noting customer impact: AcmeApps saw ~30% request failures during the 8m peak window. We'll include details in comms.

emma_support: I've scheduled a follow-up call with AcmeApps for 1700 UTC to walk through the mitigations.

maya_runtime: Dumping a short log excerpt for the RCA: ```
2025-04-12T14:12:01Z scale-loop error: quota limit returned by provider (limit=32, requested=36)
2025-04-12T14:12:07Z dispatcher queue length=18000
2025-04-12T14:16:22Z kvcache: hot_prefix_cache hitrate 0.62 -> 0.85 after patch
```

sarah_oncall: Marking this incident as mitigated. Will update PD and schedule postmortem. Closing thread here, continuing RCA in #eng-sre once logs collected.

jake_sre: leaving final note: consider pre-warming reserve capacity for sustained traffic spikes, and add quota alarms to avoid silent failures in scale-controller.

incident-bot: Incident closed by sarah_oncall at 1756665123."
